items.title: AI Review Gate Neutralizer pins required ai-reviewers context to neutral, blocking merge
items.body:
## Shape

Ruleset requires `ai-reviewers` success. The AI Review Gate Neutralizer (`.github/workflows/ai-review-gate-neutralizer.yml`) posts a fresh `neutral` `ai-reviewers` check-run each time a gate run completes with `success` on a head that also has cancelled gate suites.

## What happens

1. Several PR-head events land in the gate's concurrency group; some queued runs settle `cancelled`.
2. A gate run on the final head completes `success`.
3. The neutralizer fires on that completion and posts a NEW `neutral` check-run with a `completed_at` a few seconds AFTER the success run.
4. Rulesets evaluate the LATEST check-run per context. `neutral` does not satisfy a required status check, so `mergeable_state` stays `blocked` forever.
5. Re-running the gate repeats the cycle: success, then a newer neutral stamp.

Merged via admin bypass after a real positive verdict existed on the head SHA (PR #2706, observed on 2026-08-19: success 15:08:30Z, neutral 15:08:40Z). Heads with no cancelled suites never see a neutral stamp, which is why most PRs merge fine.

## Fix direction

The neutralizer's clear of the cancelled suite must not leave a `neutral` run as the newest entry for the required context. Either:

- target and update the OLDER cancelled check-run (keep `completed_at` older than the covering success), or
- skip posting when the head's newest `ai-reviewers` check-run is already the positive verdict and no cancelled suite is newer than it.

items.title: Claude Chat rejects Remnic MCP tools because advertised names use dots
items.body:
Claude Chat rejects Remnic MCP tools. The advertised names use dots.

KingyWolf reported this on 2026-07-24 in discussion #263. I missed it for almost a month.

## What happens

Remnic 9.22.2 (still true on current main) advertises tools as `remnic.recall`, `remnic.briefing`, and so on.

Claude Code inside Claude Desktop loads them. It rewrites the dot to an underscore before the Anthropic validator.

Claude Chat inside the same app fails with:

```
tools.236.FrontendRemoteMcpToolDefinition.name: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$'
```

That pattern is the Anthropic tool-use spec. Dots are not allowed.

## What is not a workaround

`emitLegacyTools` does not emit `remnic_*` names. It only shows or hides `engram.*` aliases.

The config text and `docs/RENAME.md` talk about `remnic_*`. The code uses `CANONICAL_MCP_PREFIX = "remnic."`. That mismatch is what sent KingyWolf looking for a setting that does not exist.

## Fix

Advertise `remnic_*` names that match `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$`.

Keep `remnic.*` callable so existing clients do not break.

Fix the docs so they stop claiming `remnic_*` is already the advertised form.

## Check

Claude Chat in Claude Desktop can load the Remnic MCP server without that validation error.

KingyWolf offered to retest.

items.title: Source-grounding filter drops non-English extraction output (CJK scripts)
items.body:
## Shape

Config: default `extractionSourceGroundingEnabled: true` (config.ts). The
source-grounding filter (`packages/remnic-core/src/extraction-source-grounding-rules.ts`)
tokenizes with whitespace/punctuation delimiters (`groundingLexemes`) and
compares whole stemmed tokens (`containsContiguousGroundingTokens`).

For languages written without spaces between words (Japanese, Chinese, Korean),
this silently drops extraction output before persistence:

1. **Paraphrased facts.** Extraction output naturally rewrites inflected or
   polite forms (飲みます → 飲む, subject 私 → ユーザー). The rewritten sentence is
   one large token per clause, so lexical token overlap with the source turn
   fails and `filterGroundedFact` drops the fact. Result: `facts: []` for a
   fully grounded statement.
2. **Entity names.** `isGroundedEntityName` requires the name to appear as a
   contiguous standalone token sequence. A CJK name embedded in a sentence
   (the normal case — names are not space-delimited) never matches, so the
   entity is dropped even when the name appears verbatim inside a source
   sentence.

## Consequence

Memories from non-whitespace-script conversations are silently discarded at
extraction time. This is the same data-loss class as #2190 (lexical mismatch
between memory and recall), one stage earlier: the memory never reaches
storage at all.

## Reproduce

Local-LLM extraction fixture: a conversation in Japanese, a mocked extraction
response whose fact content paraphrases the source turn (or whose entity name
is embedded in a CJK sentence). `ExtractionEngine.extract()` returns
`facts: []` / `entities: []` with no failure marker — the drop is silent.

Verbatim-substring facts still pass, which is why the gap is easy to miss in
English-only fixtures (English paraphrase survives via per-word token overlap).

## Also blocks

Any cross-script entity-alias extraction contract (canonical source-script
name + transliterated alias, as reviewed on PR #2508) is blocked until
grounding handles non-whitespace scripts; aliases would be dropped by the
same filter.

## Suggested direction

Script-aware tokenization (or substring/n-gram matching for scripts without
spaces) inside `groundingLexemes`/`isGroundedEntityName`, gated and tested
per script class. Out of scope for the #2190 prompt-policy fix.

items.title: refactor(plugins): share Codex/Claude hook runner; schema-drive Hermes register

labels.name: agent-review
labels.description: Issue intended for an AI coding agent review

items.body:
Part of #2467 (audit S17). **Deferred.** Real duplication, large CJS extract. Do not start until first slices #2468–#2474 are done.

## Problem

`plugin-claude-code` and `plugin-codex` each ship a long hook runner. Most of the HTTP/session logic is the same. Claude Code is missing daemon URL/HTTPS handling that Codex already has.

Hermes `register()` is a long suffix list plus duplicated `remnic_*` / `engram_*` registration. `provider.get_tool_schemas()` already exists and is unused by that loop.

## Evidence

- `packages/plugin-claude-code/hooks/bin/remnic-cc-hook.cjs` — ~958 lines; comment that it mirrors Codex; hard-coded host/port; client id `claude-code`.
- `packages/plugin-codex/hooks/bin/remnic-codex-hook.cjs` — ~1238 lines; `REMNIC_DAEMON_URL`; PreCompact + session-end materialize.
- `packages/plugin-hermes/remnic_hermes/__init__.py` — suffix lists + `_register_issue_*` helpers + manual `register_tool` ×2.
- `packages/plugin-hermes/remnic_hermes/provider.py` — `get_tool_schemas()` / `_handler_name_for_tool()`.

## Change (when you pick this up)

1. One parameterized hook runner. Thin wrappers set client id, connector priority, and Codex-only events. Claude Code must inherit daemon URL/HTTPS.
2. Hermes `register()` loops `get_tool_schemas()`. Keep issue-815 hooks and host-config load as they are.

## Out of scope

Merging `hermes-provider` with `plugin-hermes/client.py`. Duplicate `skills/` trees. `plugin-pi` publishers (already share a base).

## Validation

Existing hook tests for both hosts. Claude Code hook must honor `REMNIC_DAEMON_URL` the same way Codex does. Hermes still registers both `remnic.*` and `engram.*` names.

## Depends on

#2467 first slices. Optional relative to #2470 (plugin-id).

items.title: refactor(access): one zod wire schema and boundary dispatch for recall/observe

labels.name: agent-review
labels.description: Issue intended for an AI coding agent review

items.body:
Part of #2467 (audit S04). **Large blast. Do not start until first slices on #2467 have landed.**

## Problem

Access operations are modeled three times: zod wire schemas, parallel TS interfaces on `EngramAccessService`, and loose boundary `strictSchema` plus manual coercion. HTTP recall/observe claim boundary dispatch but still call `this.service.recall` / `observe` directly. MCP recall skips `parseMcpRequest`.

## Evidence

- Canonical zod: `packages/remnic-core/src/access-schema.ts` (`recallRequestSchema`, `observeRequestSchema`, `memoryStoreRequestSchema`).
- Parallel interfaces: `access-service.ts` (`EngramAccessRecallRequest`, `EngramAccessObserveRequest`).
- HTTP `memory_store` is the target pattern (`getOperation().run()` after `readValidatedBody`).
- HTTP recall/observe bypass that pattern.
- MCP observe uses `parseMcpRequest`; recall falls through to raw args.

## Change

1. Derive service request types from zod (`z.infer` + transport overlay only).
2. Point batch/boundary `strictSchema` at those zod schemas (no missing fields such as `codingContext` / `idempotencyKey`).
3. HTTP recall + observe use the same dispatch as `memory_store`.
4. MCP recall uses `parseMcpRequest('recall', args)`.

Keep `namespace` + `effectiveNamespace` on observe responses (#1495 compat).

## Out of scope

Splitting `access-recall-surface.ts` further. Browse CLI still calling `memoryBrowse` (no boundary op).

## Validation

`access-http.test.ts`, `access-mcp.test.ts`, `access-surface-catalog.test.ts`, namespace/observe tests. Invalid recall body must 400 on HTTP and MCP, not silently default.

## Depends on

First slices on #2467. Prefer after the recall snapshot child if both are in flight (shared access files).

## Problem

Hot / episode / rule cache getters repeat the same version + TTL check. A fix in one getter can miss the others.

## Evidence

`packages/remnic-core/src/memory-cache.ts` — three getters (~36–56, ~176–193, ~214–230).

## Change

One `getVersionedCacheEntry` helper. Keep per-layer keys and invalidation as they are (#1535 / #1904). Do not rename invalidation functions in this PR.

## Validation

`memory-cache-hot.test.ts` and any episode/rule cache tests. Version mismatch and TTL expiry on each layer still miss.

## Depends on

None.

labels.name: agent-review
labels.description: Issue intended for an AI coding agent review

items.body:
Part of #2467 (audit S23).

## Problem

Semantic dedup keeps a `NEGATION_WORDS` list and a separate strip-negation regex. Adding a word to one and not the other changes match identity.

## Evidence

`packages/remnic-core/src/dedup/index.ts` (~248–325): word list and regex encode the same vocabulary twice.

## Change

Build the strip regex from `NEGATION_WORDS` (escape literals). One source.

Do not change `dedup/semantic.ts` connector-aware scan.

## Validation

`dedup/index.test.ts` and `dedup/semantic.test.ts`. Add a word to the list in a unit test and assert the strip path sees it.

## Depends on

None.

labels.name: agent-review

items.body:
Part of #2467 (audit S13).

## Problem

Chat CLI builds the engine and appends transcript itself. HTTP/MCP go through `processChatMessage`, which persists pending plan / promotion. CLI skips that.

## Evidence

- `packages/remnic-core/src/chat/chat-factory.ts` — `processChatMessage` (~78–163) including `markPendingPlan` / `markPlanResolved` / `markPendingPromotion`.
- `packages/remnic-core/src/chat/chat-cli.ts` — inline engine + `appendTranscriptEntry` for `--once` and interactive turns.

## Change

Route `--once` and interactive turns through `processChatMessage`.

Do not merge `escapeLike` / `escapeSqlLike` in this PR.

## Validation

`chat-cli.test.ts` plus a case that a pending plan written over CLI is visible the same way as HTTP.

## Depends on

None.

Part of #2467 (audit S14).

## Problem

`@remnic/coding-graph` is loaded twice (two caches, two contract checks). Track A surfaces copy the same enabled/visible gate.

## Evidence

- `packages/remnic-core/src/coding/optional-coding-graph.ts` — documented à-la-carte loader.
- `packages/remnic-core/src/coding/codegraph-runtime.ts` — parallel `loadCodegraphModule` (~273–308) with a weaker structural check.
- Gate copies: `architecture-surfaces.ts`, `decision-surfaces.ts`, `session-delta-surfaces.ts`.

## Change

1. Runtime consumes the optional-coding-graph loader only.
2. Add `isCodingKnowledgeFeatureEnabled` / `isCodingKnowledgeFeatureVisible` next to the config parser. Replace the three copies.

Do not touch `work/**` or coding-graph SQL schema layering.

## Validation

Existing coding-graph surface tests and optional-package miss tests (install hint, not `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`).

## Depends on

None.

items.title: refactor(reconcile): share plan ordering and census validators

labels.name: agent-review
labels.description: Issue intended for an AI coding agent review

items.body:
Part of #2467 (audit S12).

## Problem

Reconcile plan ordering and semantic-agreement keys are copied in three files. Census SHA-256 and `mtimeMs` validators are copied between offline-sync and reconcile. Drift is a silent converge bug.

## Evidence

- Comparator: `packages/remnic-core/src/reconcile/plan.ts` vs `manifest.ts`.
- Semantic key: `reconcile/cursor.ts` vs `manifest.ts`.
- SHA / mtime: `offline-sync.ts` `assertSha256` / `assertOfflineSyncMtimeMs` vs `reconcile/plan.ts` `assertDigest` / `assertMtimeMs`. Both use `OFFLINE_SYNC_MAX_MTIME_MS`.

## Change

1. Export `compareReconcilePlanEntries` and `semanticAgreementKey` from `reconcile/plan.ts`. Import in cursor + manifest. Delete local copies.
2. Share census validators. Keep error types (`Error` vs `ReconcilePlanInputError`) via thin wrappers.

Do not merge snapshot apply vs changeset apply.

## Validation

`reconcile/plan.test.ts`, `cursor.test.ts`, `manifest.test.ts`, offline-sync tests. Same fixture order and reject cases on both sides.

## Depends on

None.
